summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' challenge at START Hack Munich by building a product that watches Soony's supplier data drops, finds hidden launch risks, and acts on them. In the final stretch before the Sun 12:00 hand-in, the user wanted role-split UX for the buyer and head of procurement, a merged teammate branch, and a polished demo.
summary.outcome: Built and demoed an agent loop (poll, read, recompute, act) that found the real launch gaps (overbooked art books, failed statues, game cards short) and acted on them. Added separate Felix/Maren sign-ins with their own inbox, menu and History page, merged PR #8 with a conflict fix, and renamed the product Lighthouse. The last role-label and 'Fixed today' work was still in progress, and nothing from the latest commits was pushed.

repo: The portal API has only files list, single file and archive.zip, with no webhooks; changes must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256, and files are replaced under the same name.
Live (:8000) polls the portal; the demo (:8001) runs without a portal token on purpose, so the 'Watching' heartbeat must be hidden there.

Portal data under data/ is confidential and gitignored, but the llm-task-update branch carried 335 data/portal files and PR #8 merged them into main; removal needs `git rm -r --cached data/portal`, and history keeps them.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change; `entire status` and `entire brain status` are required before pushes.
Outbox sync must append under api._lock, or it overwrites actions written meanwhile.
Order exports can be cp1252 and use ';' delimiters, so readers need encoding and delimiter fallbacks.
Maren's 'approve' button must be derived from the policy approver; a generic 'ask to approve' label is wrong for her.

code.finding: The only merge conflict between llm-task-update and main: both sides added new tests at the same spot, resolved by keeping both.
New History page showing who decided what, how and when, grouped by day, up to 200 entries.

workflow: Run read-only checks and tests in a separate worktree (../ask-soony-llm-task-update) so the live and demo servers running from main are not disturbed.
Always ask before pushing to a teammate's branch, and run the Entire checks first.
Experiments that could send real supplier emails must run on state copies, never by approving cards on live data.
When a proposed feature turns out to duplicate existing UI, check the existing UI first and drop or replace it, as happened with the 'Covered' line becoming 'Fixed today'.

friction: Retrieving a teammate's branch repeatedly (several pulls) while the user was unsure whether it had arrived.
The 'Not checked since 08:30' heartbeat looked broken on the demo because that instance never polls.
The user interrupted a role-title change because they wanted the role added next to the name, not replacing it, and Maren's button read 'ask Maren to approve'.
The demo's background loop does not auto-raise call alerts, so a manual card_alerts.tick is needed.
Realtime phone calls cut off early because of background noise, concurrent responses and sideband disconnects.
open_items: Push main (several commits ahead of origin: sign-in split, History, heartbeat fix, approver inbox, Lighthouse rename); the user asks before every push.
Restart the live server so the sign-in choice, 'Waiting for your OK' and the heartbeat appear.
Finish role display (name plus role in the top right) and the Maren direct-Approve fix, then build the green 'Fixed today' list on Launch.
Remove the 335 portal data files from main (`git rm -r --cached data/portal`) if the team agrees.
Build the 6-slide pitch deck and the video (at most 3 minutes) for the 12:00 hand-in, using Lio facts, the network map and Maren's quote.
Switch the OpenAI webhook back to https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev/hooks/openai after the demo.
Optional: delete the duplicate routine, fix the demo background call-alert loop, add a top bar for Maren, and review the new pages in a browser.
